strategy_title: TF32 + Larger Tiles Regresses When Register/SMEM Pressure Dominates
strategy_description: Enabling TF32 (allow_tf32=True) and simultaneously increasing tile sizes (BLOCK_M/N/K from 32 to 64) caused a 2.2x regression despite the kernel being compute-underutilized. The larger tiles doubled dynamic shared memory per block (16 KB → 65 KB) and doubled registers per thread (64 → 128), which collapsed theoretical occupancy from 50% to 18.75% and caused the block limit to shift from registers to shared memory. Critically, executed instructions increased 3.4x (1.4M → 4.8M) while achieved occupancy remained unchanged at 6.25%, meaning the GPU was doing far more work per block with no additional parallelism to hide latency. The SharedMemoryConflicts rule persisted at ~77% bank conflict rate, indicating the larger tiles did not resolve the underlying access pattern problem.
slow_pseudocode:
# BEFORE: smaller tiles, lower register/smem pressure
BLOCK_M = 32; BLOCK_N = 32; BLOCK_K = 32
ALLOW_TF32 = False
# registers_per_thread=64, dynamic_smem=16KB, theoretical_occ=50%
acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)
fast_pseudocode:
# AFTER (regressed): larger tiles, higher register/smem pressure
BLOCK_M = 64; BLOCK_N = 64; BLOCK_K = 64
ALLOW_TF32 = False  # NOTE: TF32 flag was NOT actually changed in the diff!
# registers_per_thread=128, dynamic_smem=65KB, theoretical_occ=18.75%
acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)
applicable_when: Never apply this combined strategy (larger tiles + TF32) when the kernel is already register-limited (Block Limit Registers is the binding constraint) and theoretical occupancy is already ≤50%. The tile size increase will double register pressure and shared memory usage, collapsing occupancy further.
do_not_apply_when: Do not increase BLOCK_M/N/K when registers_per_thread is already at or near 64 and the kernel is register-limited (Block Limit Registers < Block Limit Warps). Do not increase tile sizes when SharedMemoryConflicts bank conflict rate is ~77%—larger tiles amplify the conflict count proportionally without fixing the access pattern. Do not apply when grid_size < sm_count (already wave-limited); larger tiles reduce grid size further, worsening wave coverage.
framework_notes: In Triton, BLOCK_M/N/K constexprs directly control tile size and thus register allocation and shared memory usage. Doubling all three dimensions increases register file usage ~2x and shared memory ~4x (for double-buffering), which can catastrophically reduce theoretical occupancy on SM90 (H200) where Block Limit Shared Mem becomes the binding constraint. The ALLOW_TF32 flag in the diff was NOT actually changed to True despite the plan—the regression is entirely attributable to the tile size increase and resulting resource pressure.

strategy_title: Autotuning num_warps/num_stages Without Tile Size Increases Regresses
strategy_description: When the plan called for larger BLOCK_M/BLOCK_K tile sizes but the actual diff only changed num_warps and num_stages while increasing BLOCK_M from 32→64 and BLOCK_K from 32→64 as hardcoded constants (not autotuned), the result was higher register pressure (64→96 registers/thread), lower theoretical occupancy (50%→31.25%), doubled instruction count (1.4M→2.5M), and 90% longer kernel duration (30.4→57.82 µs). The achieved occupancy remained identical at 6.25% because the grid size was unchanged (still 62 blocks on 132 SMs), while the larger tiles simply did more work per block without improving SM coverage. Bank conflicts worsened (12-way→17.9-way) because the larger shared memory tiles amplified the existing conflict pattern rather than resolving it.
slow_pseudocode:
# Before: small fixed tiles, low register pressure
BLOCK_M = 32; BLOCK_K = 32
# grid = 62 blocks, 64 regs/thread, 16KB smem/block
@triton.jit
def kernel(...):
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr = 32
    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr = 32
    ...
applicable_when: Never — this is a negative example. Do not apply this pattern.
do_not_apply_when: When the grid is already too small (waves_per_sm < 0.1) and the root cause is insufficient blocks: increasing tile sizes as hardcoded constants without making them autotune parameters does not increase grid coverage and only adds register/smem pressure. Autotuning only num_warps/num_stages while keeping tile sizes fixed inside the kernel body is ineffective when the bottleneck is grid underutilization.
framework_notes: In Triton, tile size constexprs (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K) must be placed inside the @triton.autotune configs dict to be swept by the autotuner. Placing them as hardcoded constexprs inside the kernel body while only sweeping num_warps/num_stages means the autotuner cannot explore different tile sizes. The key=[] in the autotune decorator also means the autotuner does not re-tune for different problem sizes. To fix grid underutilization, tile sizes must be passed as kernel arguments or placed in the autotune config dict, and the grid lambda must be updated to use META['BLOCK_M'] etc.

strategy_title: TMA Block Pointers Without Tile Resize Worsen Bank Conflicts
strategy_description: Replacing scalar pointer arithmetic with tl.make_block_ptr / tl.advance while keeping the same fixed tile sizes (BLOCK_M=32, BLOCK_N=32, BLOCK_K=32) and only autotuning num_warps/num_stages caused a 1.69x slowdown. The warp cycles per issued instruction jumped from 7.38 to 21.7, and shared memory bank conflicts worsened from 12-way (77.78% of wavefronts) to 17-way (82.35% of wavefronts), indicating that the TMA descriptor layout interacted poorly with the existing shared memory access pattern. The autotune configs in this attempt did not vary BLOCK_M or BLOCK_K (all configs had empty dicts {}), so no tile-size exploration occurred and the grid size remained unchanged at 62 blocks — the root cause of low occupancy was never addressed.
slow_pseudocode:
# BEFORE: scalar pointer arithmetic, fixed tiles
for k_idx in range(cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    a = tl.load(A + (offs_k[None,:] + k_idx*BLOCK_K) + 512*offs_a_m[:,None])
    b = tl.load(B + ...)
    acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)
fast_pseudocode:
# AFTER (regressed): TMA block pointers, same tile sizes, autotune only varies num_warps/num_stages
# autotune configs: triton.Config({}, num_warps=8, num_stages=4), ... (no BLOCK_M/BLOCK_K variation)
A_ptr = tl.make_block_ptr(base=A, shape=(M,K), strides=(stride_am,stride_ak),
    offsets=(pid_m*BLOCK_M, 0), block_shape=(BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K), order=(1,0))
B_ptr = tl.make_block_ptr(base=B, shape=(K,N), strides=(stride_bk,stride_bn),
    offsets=(0, pid_n*BLOCK_N), block_shape=(BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N), order=(0,1))
for _ in range(cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    a = tl.load(A_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1))
    b = tl.load(B_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1))
    acc = tl.dot(a, b, acc, allow_tf32=False)
    A_ptr = tl.advance(A_ptr, (0, BLOCK_K))
    B_ptr = tl.advance(B_ptr, (BLOCK_K, 0))
applicable_when: Never apply this pattern in isolation — TMA block pointers alone without tile size changes do not resolve shared memory bank conflicts.
do_not_apply_when: Do not switch to tl.make_block_ptr without simultaneously varying BLOCK_M and BLOCK_K in the autotune configs. If the autotune config dicts are empty ({}), no tile exploration occurs and the bank conflict pattern is unchanged or worsened. Avoid this when the kernel already has severe bank conflicts (>70% wavefronts affected) and a grid smaller than SM count — the TMA path alone does not fix either issue.
framework_notes: In Triton, @triton.autotune configs must include the tile-size constexprs (e.g., BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K) as keys in the Config dict for autotuning to actually explore different tile shapes. Passing empty dicts triton.Config({}, num_warps=N, num_stages=S) only varies warp count and pipeline depth, leaving tile geometry fixed. tl.make_block_ptr uses Hopper TMA hardware (sm_90+) but the shared memory layout it produces can have different bank conflict characteristics than scalar loads — verify bank conflict metrics after switching.

strategy_title: Autotuning num_warps/num_stages without changing tile sizes regresses
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune that only varies num_warps and num_stages—without changing BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K—caused a 27% regression. The autotune selected a configuration (BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=16, BLOCK_K=64) that was hardcoded in the kernel body rather than passed as parameters, so the tile sizes did not actually change across configs; instead, the larger hardcoded tiles (128x16x64 vs original 32x32x32) dramatically increased register pressure (64→116 registers/thread) and shared memory usage (16→74 KB/block), which crushed theoretical occupancy from 50% to 18.75% and more than doubled total instruction count (1.4M→2.6M). The achieved occupancy remained stuck at 6.25% while elapsed cycles grew 27%, yielding a net slowdown despite a modest improvement in L2 hit rate (27%→58%) and reduced warp stall cycles per instruction (7.4→5.2).
applicable_when: Never apply autotune that only varies num_warps/num_stages when the real bottleneck is tile size (bank conflicts, occupancy limited by registers/shared memory from oversized tiles).
do_not_apply_when: Do not add @triton.autotune with empty config dicts (no tile size keys) when the kernel has hardcoded BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K as constexpr body assignments—the tile sizes will not change across configs, but a single bad hardcoded tile choice will dominate and may increase register pressure and shared memory, reducing occupancy and increasing instruction count.
framework_notes: In Triton, @triton.autotune can only vary parameters that are passed as kernel signature arguments with tl.constexpr type. Tile sizes hardcoded as `BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr = 32` inside the kernel body are NOT tunable—they are compile-time constants baked into a single JIT compilation. To make tile sizes tunable, they must appear in the kernel signature (e.g., `def kernel(..., BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr)`) and be listed as keys in the Config dicts. The grid lambda must also reference META['BLOCK_M'] etc. to adapt to the chosen config.

strategy_title: Transposed B Load + Smaller BLOCK_M Worsens Bank Conflicts
strategy_description: Changing the B matrix load from stride-24 column-major [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] to transposed row-major [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K] with tl.trans() before tl.dot, combined with reducing BLOCK_M from 128 to 32 and BLOCK_N from 16 to 64, caused a 1.7x regression. Despite reducing registers per thread (116→96) and dynamic shared memory (73.7→49.1 KB/block), the bank conflict way count worsened from 12-way to 17-way and the conflict wavefront percentage increased from 74.9% to 82.28%. The L2 hit rate dropped sharply (57.7%→36.1%) and warp cycles per issued instruction increased (5.21→7.2), indicating the new access pattern introduced new local memory spills (MemoryCacheAccessPattern rule triggered for local loads/stores at 41.38% speedup potential) and did not resolve the shared memory bank conflict root cause.
slow_pseudocode:
# BEFORE: stride-24 B load, BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=16
BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr = 128
BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr = 16
# inside k_idx loop:
idx_m = offs_k[:, None] + k_idx * BLOCK_K  # [BLOCK_K, 1]
idx_n = offs_b_n[None, :]                   # [1, BLOCK_N]
xindex = idx_n + 24 * idx_m                 # stride-24 -> 12-way bank conflicts
b = tl.load(B + tl.broadcast_to(idx_m + 512*idx_n, [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N]))
acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)
fast_pseudocode:
# AFTER (regressed): transposed B load, BLOCK_M=32, BLOCK_N=64
BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr = 32
BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr = 64
# inside k_idx loop:
idx_n_bt = offs_b_n[:, None]                      # [BLOCK_N, 1]
idx_k_bt = offs_k[None, :] + k_idx * BLOCK_K      # [1, BLOCK_K]
mask_b = (idx_n_bt < N)
b_T = tl.load(B + (idx_k_bt + 512 * idx_n_bt),    # [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K], stride=1 in K
              mask=mask_b, other=0.0)
acc += tl.dot(a, tl.trans(b_T), allow_tf32=False)  # 17-way bank conflicts, worse!
applicable_when: Never apply this pattern in isolation — transposing the B load order does not resolve shared memory bank conflicts when the conflict originates from the shared memory layout of the accumulator or A tile, not the B load itself.
do_not_apply_when: Do not transpose the B matrix load (loading [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K] then calling tl.trans()) when the SharedMemoryConflicts rule is triggered and the bank conflict way count is already ≥12. This approach changes the global memory access pattern but does not change the shared memory layout that causes bank conflicts. Avoid when BLOCK_N is large (64) relative to the number of banks (32) — the transposed layout can introduce new bank conflict patterns. Do not apply when the kernel already has local memory spill risk (registers_per_thread > 96); tl.trans() on large tiles can increase register pressure and trigger local memory spills (evidenced by MemoryCacheAccessPattern rule for local loads/stores).
framework_notes: In Triton, tl.trans() on a [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K] tensor before tl.dot does not change how the data is laid out in shared memory — it only reorders the logical view. The bank conflict pattern in shared memory is determined by how threads write the loaded data into shared memory, which depends on the tile shape and thread indexing, not the logical transpose. Changing BLOCK_N from 16 to 64 while keeping BLOCK_K=64 creates a 64x64 B tile in shared memory, which with 32 banks can produce systematic conflicts depending on the stride. The MemoryCacheAccessPattern rule appearing after (not before) the change indicates new local memory spills introduced by the larger BLOCK_N tile and tl.trans() register pressure.
